title: Every problem, a lesson.
text: A correct answer is only the beginning. For a student, the harder question is often: how did we get there? Ember turns a STEM question into a blackboard lesson, with writing, narration, chapters, and space for follow-up questions. This is our working prototype for introductory university learning.

title: Start with the question.
text: Start in the studio and enter a problem. Here, we use integration by parts: the integral of x times e to the two x. Guest access lets you explore without creating an account. In this prepared walkthrough, we are using Ember's production interface components. The generation sequence is condensed, not a claim about processing speed.

title: Follow the reasoning.
text: The lesson is not a stack of slides. Ember compiles structured board actions into strokes on a persistent blackboard. In this reviewed chapter excerpt, choosing u equals x gives d u equals d x. Differentiating the polynomial makes the remaining work simpler. The writing you see comes from the same rendering engine used in the application.

title: Your pace. Your next question.
text: The player provides pause, seeking, playback speed, and chapter navigation. You can return to a step instead of starting the explanation again. Office Hours is the follow-up workspace: ask why a formula applies, request a simpler explanation, or ask for a board adjustment. The exchange shown here is a prepared example, not a live model response.

title: One lesson. A coordinated crew.
text: Behind the lesson is a coordinated multi-agent pipeline. A director plans the learning arc. A transcript planner writes the spoken explanation. Parallel scene writers choreograph board actions against that transcript. A scene reviewer checks the work, with a bounded repair attempt when review fails. Deterministic checks inspect supported arithmetic and board layout. An independent solver provides an additional answer comparison. These checks reduce risk; they do not prove every lesson is correct.

title: From structured actions to ink and voice.
text: Accepted scenes are compiled into a seekable board timeline. Writing and speech are coordinated through narration anchors, audio timing, and explicit pauses. Voice synthesis is queued and cached. Alignment quality can vary, and the prototype reports timing issues rather than claiming perfect synchronization. The important design choice is that the explanation and the board share a lesson structure.

title: Questions worth sharing.
text: The community gallery makes shared questions discoverable. Search by topic, open a lesson, and explore an explanation someone else has already created. Today, gallery posts store lesson scripts; replay can still request narration. Our next step is durable saved audio and timing, so a growing library can become reliably ready to replay. That is the direction, not a claim that the library is already complete.

title: Every problem, a lesson.
text: Today, Ember turns a question into a lesson students can follow and revisit. Next, we want to make those lessons reusable across a growing library, bring Ember into educational platforms through an API, and add live tutoring alongside structured explanations. Ember. Every problem, a lesson.
